Rejection probabilities of a group sequential design with two endpoints

Source: R/gs_prob_mtp.R
gs_prob_mtp.Rd

For the standardized statistics of two endpoints with a joint multivariate normal distribution, computes under a multiple testing procedure the probability of rejecting each null hypothesis at each look, the probability of rejecting both and the probability of rejecting at least one.

Usage

gs_prob_mtp(
  upper,
  lower = NULL,
  mean = 0,
  sigma,
  analysis = NULL,
  mtp = c("fixed_sequence", "bonferroni"),
  hierarchical = c("overall", "stagewise"),
  upper_recycled = NULL
)

Arguments

upper

List of two numeric vectors: the efficacy bounds of the first and of the second endpoint at their looks (Inf for no efficacy test at a look).

lower

Futility bounds of the first endpoint at its looks (-Inf for none), or NULL for no futility bounds.

mean

Mean vector of the statistics, first the looks of the first endpoint and then those of the second (recycled if of length 1).

sigma

Covariance matrix of the statistics in the same order, for example sigma of lr_cov with two endpoints.

analysis

List of two integer vectors: the analysis at which each look of the first and of the second endpoint takes place (strictly increasing within an endpoint; equal numbers mean the same analysis). NULL means that both endpoints are tested at analyses 1 to K.

mtp

"fixed_sequence" or "bonferroni".

hierarchical

"overall" or "stagewise" (used with mtp = "fixed_sequence").

upper_recycled

For mtp = "bonferroni", an optional list of two numeric vectors: the efficacy bounds of the first and of the second endpoint at their looks at the level after the other hypothesis has been rejected (not above upper). NULL means no recycling.

Value

A list with

looks

A data frame with one row per look: endpoint (1 or 2), look, analysis, the probability of rejecting the hypothesis of the endpoint at the look (prob_upper), its cumulative sum (cum_upper) and the probability of stopping for futility at the look (prob_lower, 0 for the second endpoint and for the last look of the first).

reject

The probabilities of rejecting the first hypothesis (first), the second (second), both (both) and at least one (any).

Details

Each endpoint is tested at its own looks, and analysis places the looks of both endpoints on one sequence of analyses; an analysis may include looks of one endpoint or of both. A hypothesis is rejected at the first look at which its statistic is at or above its efficacy bound and is not tested again. The trial stops for futility at an interim look of the first endpoint at which its hypothesis has not been rejected and its statistic is below the futility bound. The futility bound at the last look of the first endpoint is not used.

With mtp = "bonferroni", each endpoint is tested at all its looks until the trial stops, with bounds computed at levels that add up to alpha. The trial stops when both hypotheses are rejected or for futility.

With mtp = "bonferroni" and upper_recycled, the level of a rejected hypothesis is passed on to the other hypothesis (the graphical procedure of Maurer and Bretz 2013, Algorithm 1, for two hypotheses). Each hypothesis is tested with its bounds in upper until the other hypothesis is rejected, and with its bounds in upper_recycled from the analysis at which the other is rejected on: a hypothesis rejected with its bound in upper at an analysis makes the other be tested with its bound in upper_recycled at the same analysis. The bounds in upper_recycled are those of the level after recycling, for example (w1 + g21 w2) alpha for the first hypothesis with the weights w and the fraction g21 of the level of the second hypothesis that is passed on to the first. They must not exceed the bounds in upper, which holds when the nominal levels of the spending function do not decrease with the level (Maurer and Bretz 2013, Section 3.1). The futility stop of the first endpoint also applies after the second hypothesis has been rejected.

With mtp = "fixed_sequence", the second hypothesis is tested only after the first has been rejected. With hierarchical = "overall" it is tested at the analysis at which the first hypothesis is rejected and at the later looks of the second endpoint, until it is rejected (strategy (b) of Glimm et al. 2010). With hierarchical = "stagewise" the trial stops at the analysis at which the first hypothesis is rejected, and the second hypothesis is tested only at that analysis (strategy (a) of Glimm et al. 2010, the procedure of Tamhane et al. 2010).

The probabilities are sums of rectangle probabilities of the multivariate normal distribution, one for each combination of the outcome of the first endpoint (rejection or stop for futility at a look, or no rejection) and the look at which the second hypothesis is rejected. With upper_recycled, the probabilities are summed over the outcomes at each analysis: at an analysis at which both hypotheses are tested and neither has been rejected, with the bounds A1, A2 in upper and B1, B2 in upper_recycled, both hypotheses are rejected when Z1 >= A1 and Z2 >= B2 or when B1 <= Z1 < A1 and Z2 >= A2, only the first when Z1 >= A1 and Z2 < B2, only the second when Z1 < B1 and Z2 >= A2, and neither when Z1 < A1 and Z2 < A2; at an analysis at which one hypothesis is tested, it is rejected or not. The futility stop splits the outcomes in which the first hypothesis is tested and not rejected at an interim look. The rectangle probabilities are computed with mvtnorm::pmvnorm() (at most 20 looks in total): with the Genz-Bretz algorithm for the rectangles that involve both endpoints and have four or more coordinates and, as in gs_prob, for the other rectangles of four or more coordinates whose covariance matrix is not that of a Markov sequence and of nine or more coordinates with two finite limits for some coordinate, for which the Miwa algorithm can be inaccurate, and with the Miwa algorithm otherwise. The Genz-Bretz algorithm uses a fixed seed, so that the results are reproducible and the random number generator of the session is not changed, and an absolute error tolerance of 1e-5 for each rectangle, which can be changed with options(DesignComplexSurvival.genz_abseps = ...).

References

Glimm E, Maurer W, Bretz F (2010). Hierarchical testing of multiple endpoints in group-sequential trials. Statistics in Medicine 29:219-228.

Maurer W, Bretz F (2013). Multiple testing in group sequential trials using graphical approaches. Statistics in Biopharmaceutical Research 5:311-320.

Tamhane AC, Mehta CR, Liu L (2010). Testing a primary and a secondary endpoint in a group sequential design. Biometrics 66:1174-1184.

See also

gs_prob, gs_bounds, lr_cov

Examples

# Two looks at information fractions 0.5 and 1 for both endpoints and
# correlation 0.5 between the endpoints
tt <- c(0.5, 1)
r <- sqrt(outer(tt, tt, pmin) / outer(tt, tt, pmax))
sigma <- rbind(cbind(r, 0.5 * r), cbind(0.5 * r, r))
b1 <- gs_bounds(tt, sf_eff = "OF")$upper
b2 <- gs_bounds(tt, sf_eff = "Pocock")$upper
gs_prob_mtp(list(b1, b2), mean = c(2, 2.9, 1.5, 2.1), sigma = sigma)$reject
#>     first    second      both       any 
#> 0.8248839 0.4412122 0.4412122 0.8248839 
# Probability of rejecting the second hypothesis when it is true
gs_prob_mtp(list(b1, b2), mean = c(2, 2.9, 0, 0), sigma = sigma)$reject
#>      first     second       both        any 
#> 0.82488393 0.02068571 0.02068571 0.82488393 
# Bonferroni with the level alpha / 2 for each endpoint and the level
# alpha after the other hypothesis has been rejected (full recycling)
h1 <- gs_bounds(tt, alpha = 0.0125, sf_eff = "OF")$upper
h2 <- gs_bounds(tt, alpha = 0.0125, sf_eff = "Pocock")$upper
gs_prob_mtp(list(h1, h2), mean = c(2, 2.9, 1.5, 2.1), sigma = sigma,
            mtp = "bonferroni", upper_recycled = list(b1, b2))$reject
#>     first    second      both       any 
#> 0.7620396 0.4654847 0.4417205 0.7858038
